scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this scenario. So the user is a man asking if he's the asshole (AITA) for asking his boyfriend to pick up and drop off his child on weekends, which led to the boyfriend suggesting a breakup.

First, I need to evaluate the moral acceptability of the action. The key points here are the responsibilities and expectations between the partners.

The man's boyfriend works full-time from 7am-7pm. The man has a weekend job from 9am-12pm, but he extended his hours to 9-5 to afford his son's football. The son is 12 and wants to play football. The man asked his boyfriend to pick up and drop off the child on weekends. The boyfriend refused, saying his dad could do it, but the man points out that the dad lives in South London and doesn't drive, so it's a longer trip for him, whereas the boyfriend lives nearby and can do it in 15 minutes.

The boyfriend got angry, saying he's working longer hours to support them, wants weekends to relax, and feels pressured. He suggested a breakup. The man's mum also sided with the boyfriend, saying he's out of line.

Now, moral acceptability: Is it wrong for the man to ask his boyfriend to help with childcare? Well, they're not living together, but they're in a relationship where they're "in and out of each other's homes." The boyfriend has been in his life for 3 years. However, the boyfriend isn't the child's parent. The man's responsibility as the parent is primary. The boyfriend's role is as a partner, not a co-parent. So expecting him to take on childcare duties, especially when he's working long hours, might be unreasonable.

The man's mum said it's his responsibility, not the boyfriend's. That's a key point. Even though the boyfriend is involved, he's not obligated to take on parental responsibilities unless he's agreed to be a co-parent. The man extended his own work hours to pay for the football, which is his choice, but then expecting the boyfriend to handle transportation might be overstepping.

The boyfriend's perspective: He's working long hours, maybe feeling stressed, and wants his weekends to relax. He's not the parent, so he might not feel responsible for the child's schedule. The man's demand could be seen as putting too much pressure on him, especially since the boyfriend's dad could do it (even if it's a longer trip, but maybe the dad is willing to help). The boyfriend might feel that the man is trying to make him take on more than he's comfortable with, especially since they're not cohabiting or married.

In terms of moral acceptability: The action of asking the boyfriend to pick up the child might be considered unreasonable because the boyfriend isn't a parent. The primary responsibility lies with the parent (the man), and while partners can help, it's not a given. The boyfriend has the right to set boundaries, especially if he's already working long hours. The man's expectation that the boyfriend should do this because he's part of the family might be misplaced. The boyfriend's reaction to suggest a breakup might be a bit harsh, but the initial request could be seen as pushing too hard.

So, the man's action of asking the boyfriend to take on this responsibility is morally unacceptable because he's placing an undue burden on someone who isn't a parent. The boyfriend isn't obligated to do it, especially when he's already working long hours. The man should handle his own child's schedule, perhaps finding other solutions like carpooling with other parents, or arranging for the dad to help even if it's a longer trip. The boyfriend's refusal is reasonable, so the man's insistence is the issue here.

Therefore, the answer should be 0 (morally unacceptable) because the man is asking for something unreasonable from his boyfriend, who isn't a parent and has his own commitments.
